title: Book Two · Chapter 183: The Job That Stays Done
story:
At Mr Sun's place, Dad is finishing a small wooden stand. The customer wants to put a heavy box on it. Dad puts the test weight in the middle and steps back.

Ronan stands near the counter. He can see all four feet of the stand. None lifts from the floor.

“Finished?” he asks.

“One more check.”

Dad moves the weight to one side. He presses the top gently, then checks the joints. Mr Sun comes over with the work card.

“Ready for tomorrow?” he asks.

“Yes. I can explain the weight limit when the customer comes.”

Mr Sun reads the note. Dad has written the size, the work time, and the agreed cost. Nothing is crossed out today.

Ronan smiles at the card. Dad notices.

“You like my handwriting?”

“It is hard work to read it.”

Mr Sun laughs and takes the card to the counter. Dad asks Ronan to bring his clean cloth. Ronan brings it from the shelf, away from the tools.

They wipe the top of the stand. The wood is plain and smooth. The customer asked for a plain finish. Dad leaves the wood without a bright coat.

“I like it this way,” Ronan says.

“So do I.”

The customer arrives the next morning. Ronan is there with Mum before they go to buy food. They stand aside while Dad explains the stand.

The customer tries his own box on it. He reads the weight note and asks about the feet. Dad shows him the flat places underneath. Then the customer pays Mr Sun and takes the stand away.

Nothing comes back through the door.

Dad watches for a moment, then puts the test weight away. Mr Sun gives him the next work card. It is another ordinary job at another agreed price.

Outside, Ronan walks beside Mum.

“That one went well,” he says.

“Yes.”

“He is good at that.”

“He is.”

She stops at a vegetable stall and chooses two firm tomatoes. Ronan holds the bag open. He wants to say more about Dad. But today he saw Dad do a good job. He is glad about that.

At home, Mum puts the food away and counts the money left from her own work payment. She keeps some for food and other things at home. She puts the rest in her own small purse.

“For your walk?” Ronan asks.

“For a book of patterns. I saw one I want.”

“With very straight lines?”

“With lines I can actually read.”

They laugh. Ronan carries her work basket to the table. Dad will come home for dinner. Mum wants to tell him about the pattern book then.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

stand＝架台；joint＝接合处；weight limit＝承重限制；plain finish＝朴素、不加装饰的表面处理。

## 理解问题

1. Dad这次的工作怎样具体显示真实能力？
2. 这次顺利交付是否意味着他已经重新开店或解决全部责任？

## 读句子

**The customer tries his own box on it.**

拆开看：The customer / tries / his own box on it.

顾客／把自己的箱子放上去／试用。
